name: Alila Manggis
positioning: Seaside resort in East Bali, set in a coconut grove between the sea and Mount Agung, with ocean-facing rooms in thatched Balinese pavilions
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet seaside base in East Bali with ocean views
Guests interested in Balinese culture, village visits and cooking experiences
Wellness seekers drawn to open-air spa treatments and sunrise-facing yoga

facts.text: Alila Manggis is a seaside resort in Manggis, East Bali, set amid a coconut grove between the sea and Mount Agung.
The resort's design is a contemporary interpretation of traditional Balinese architecture.
The Seaside King Suite is the resort's largest accommodation.
Deluxe Rooms are on the upper floor, with a private balcony and daybed looking across the coconut grove, pool and sea.
Seasalt's signature meal is the Megibung, a traditional East Bali shared feast served on a carved timber stand called the Dulang.
Seasalt serves Indonesian and Western dishes in a traditional pavilion set on a lotus pond.
The Flavors of East Bali cooking experience starts with picking ingredients in the resort's garden and cooking with a chef using the traditional firewood method.
The Caves and Crystals experience visits the Goa Lawah bat cave temple and the salt pans of Kusamba, where sea salt is still harvested by hand.
The Alila Leisure Concierge team tailors activities across five themes: Cultural Learning, Conscious Living, Active Spirits, Culinary Arts and Couple Celebration.
The resort follows a zero-waste policy and runs a coral reef conservation programme with a local diving operation.
Tenganan village, known for its double-ikat Gringsing woven cloth, is near the resort.

highlights.text: All rooms and suites face the ocean, with views across the straits to Nusa Penida.
Rooms and suites are housed in traditional two-storey thatched Balinese pavilions angled to the beach.
Spa Alila treatments take place in open-air bales facing the sea, in the shade of pandan groves.
Surya is a yoga shala overlooking the ocean on Bali's east coast, where the sun rises.
The Roots of Tenganan experience is a bike ride through rice fields to the Bali Aga village of Tenganan to meet master ikat weavers.

considerations.text: The resort is about a 90-minute drive from Ngurah Rai International Airport.
WhataHotel notes limited dining and entertainment options outside the resort.
